note: Lean names are PROPOSED. `certainty` is a claim about this author's confidence, NOT about Mathlib. Step 11 replaces it with evidence.

certainty_vocabulary.exact: believed to be a real Mathlib 4 declaration name, spelled correctly
certainty_vocabulary.uncertain: plausible but the spelling or namespace is in doubt
certainty_vocabulary.none: no Mathlib constant is expected to exist for this concept

loogle_syntax_note: Loogle accepts a bare name, a comma-separated list of constants that must all occur, a double-quoted name substring, and a type pattern with `_` holes, optionally anchored to the conclusion with `|-`. Which of these forms actually parse is measured in step 11, not assumed.

lean.name: Module
lean.why: Mathlib 4 has no `VectorSpace`; a vector space is `Module K V` with `[Field K]`

lean.name: Module.Free
lean.why: free module; every vector space is one, but it is a different statement

lean.name: DivisionRing
lean.why: the non-commutative weakening; relevant because the fixture never says K is commutative

lean.name: Module.rank
lean.why: the Cardinal-valued dimension, defined for any module

lean.name: Module.finrank
lean.why: the Nat-valued dimension; namespace is the open question -- see below

lean.name: FiniteDimensional.finrank
lean.why: the older spelling of the same declaration; one of these two is stale and I do not know which

lean.name: FiniteDimensional
lean.why: the finiteness hypothesis, not the dimension itself

concepts.open_question: finrank was moved between namespaces at some point. Both spellings are recorded so step 11 can decide by evidence instead of memory.

concepts.why: In Mathlib the domain of a linear map is a type index, not a declaration. There is nothing to anchor to.
concepts.loogle_kept_because: a query with no matching constant is still a finding: it shows the concept lives in the type, not in a name
